thread.label: Program thread
thread.note: The three figures are layers of one program, not three separate projects. FIG. 03 builds the transducer that produces the capacitance change; FIG. 02 is the readout that makes such a small change resolvable without a battery on the lens; FIG. 01 is the integrated system where both are assembled and validated ex vivo and in vivo.

projects.title: Smart contact lens for continuous intraocular pressure monitoring
projects.summary: A flexible resistive sensing film integrated into a soft contact lens and read out through an ultrathin gold antenna, so intraocular pressure can be followed continuously instead of captured once in a clinic. Lens readings are validated against a commercial tonometer ex vivo (porcine) and in vivo (rabbit). Developed within an AMED-supported medical-device R&D project; the funding is project-level, not a personal grant.

projects.title: PT-symmetric passive readout for battery-free sensing
projects.summary: Parity-time symmetric coupling sharpens the resonance of an otherwise low-Q passive tag, turning a small capacitance shift into a resolvable measurement. The approach is what allows a passive resonator on a wet, curved surface to be read without putting a battery on the lens.

projects.title: Resistive and capacitive flexible transducers
projects.summary: PEDOT-based resistive films and wrinkled-gold capacitive sensors, built with photolithography, spin coating, gold deposition, electroplating and laser processing, then characterised electrically and validated on the bench and in animal experiments.
